purpose: Performance budgets, endurance, packaging and release safety

cases.userFriction: The product should disappear into the background rather than make a low-power laptop feel heavier.

cases.workload: Continuous mixed app switching for 30 minutes
cases.userFriction: Normal use must not produce fan noise, battery drain, or visible lag.
Heavy multitasking should not cause delayed or missing timeline updates.

cases.workload: 10 browser windows, 100 total tabs, frequent active-tab changes
cases.userFriction: Browser-heavy users should not experience a noticeably heavier tracker.

cases.workload: Multiple years of aggregated history plus high-resolution recent data
cases.userFriction: A long history should remain browsable instead of turning into a frozen screen.
A long-offline laptop should catch up quietly without monopolizing CPU, disk, or network.
The product must remain boring after days of uptime, not degrade gradually.
Month-long use is the actual product experience; short benchmarks are insufficient.
First-run setup should not require understanding services or process architecture.
An update should feel routine, not like a risky database operation.
A failed update must not strand the user without tracking.
Users should understand whether uninstall removes history before they commit to it.

cases.scenario: Microsoft Store versus standalone package parity
cases.userFriction: The install channel should not change what the product records.
